scopeFindings: Backlog drain (scope item 3) is not met under the sustained-contention profile the task's own context.md measured. Worst case under a governor that never clears is exactly one RETENTION_MIN_BATCH_SIZE=50-row batch per eligible run (retention-run-budget.ts:79,91-100 latches busyTimeoutBatchGranted after the first timeout-and-still-busy batch, so every later waitForGovernor call in that run short-circuits to 'governor-busy' with zero further work; pinned by memory-retention.service.spec.ts:1531-1572, 'under sustained contention runs one minimum slow batch then stops'). At the hourly cron cadence ('17 * * * *', thoth-runtime/src/lib/memory-retention-job.ts:43) that is 50 rows/hour in the best sub-case (host lagging but not foreground-active): 171,524 / 50 = 3,430.48 -> 3,431 runs -> ~3,431 hours -> ~142.9 days (~4.8 months) to drain. If foreground activity ALSO stays continuously high (the actual host state in context.md: 7 concurrent sessions, gate 'essentially always busy'), memory-retention.service.ts:239-264's foregroundMaxConsecutiveSkips=2 only lets 1 run in every 3 hourly ticks reach execute() at all, so the realistic worst case on the reporting host is ~3x worse: ~10,293 hours (~14.3 months). This is not a code defect -- the run is bounded and safe by design -- but scope item 3 ('provide a way to drain the existing 171,524-row/878 MB backlog') is not satisfied for the host that raised the task; it is satisfied only once contention subsides, which the implementer's own comments (memory-retention-config.ts:93-100) treat as an accepted trade rather than a solved drain path.

CLAUDE.md's 'Gates, in order' bullet (memory-curator/CLAUDE.md, the 'Retention never writes processed_at...' paragraph) still lists 'foreground-active (5 min)' as an unqualified gate and was not touched this round, even though memory-retention.service.ts:239-264 now adds a stateful escape (RETENTION_FOREGROUND_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_SKIPS=2) that forces a run through on the 3rd consecutive eligible tick. A reader of that bullet alone would still conclude the gate can starve retention forever, which round 1's own defect 2 and this round's context.md both show was the real failure mode being fixed. Minor documentation gap, not a logic defect (the governor bullet a few lines below WAS updated correctly).

mentorNote: The round-1 defect is bounded, not eliminated: BackgroundWorkGovernor.isClear() still cannot distinguish 'foreground-busy, safe to nudge in' from 'lagging, event loop already slow' (background-work-governor.ts:479-481), and retention-run-budget.ts:87-100 still dispatches into that undifferentiated busy state on a still-busy timeout. What changed is the blast radius: round 1 could barge in on essentially every one of ~100 per-run waitForGovernor calls at up to full batch size; round 2's busyTimeoutBatchGranted latch (retention-run-budget.ts:79,92) allows exactly ONE minimum-size (50-row) batch per run, proven by the new spec to cost up to ~1.7s of main-thread time under the host's own measured worst-case SQLite duration, then stops cold. That is a legitimate, honestly-documented engineering trade (one small bounded stall per hour beats indefinite livelock), not a fix of the governor's blind spot -- and it is why the backlog still takes months, not the '4 runs' round 1 claimed, to drain under the exact contention profile the task was filed for. Track scope item 3 as a follow-up (e.g. a size-aware or explicitly one-shot backfill path outside the hourly budget) rather than assuming this PR closes it.
